title: Who a minion attacks
assumed: Lane minions attack enemy minions before shapers, but turn on a shaper who hurts one of their team's shapers nearby.
lookFor: Whether enemy minions keep hitting your minions while you stand among them, and whether they turn on you at once when you hit an enemy shaper near them.

title: Lane minions and shapers
assumed: A lane minion attacks towers and enemy minions before any shaper, and goes for a shaper only when nothing else is in reach or that shaper just hit one of its team's shapers.
lookFor: Minions ignoring a shaper who stands among them until that shaper hits one of their team's shapers, and leaving a shaper who walks away.

title: How far a lane minion chases a shaper
assumed: A lane minion chasing a shaper gives up after about 3 seconds or 20 units, walks back to its lane and ignores that shaper for a few seconds.
lookFor: How long and how far an enemy wave follows you when you walk away from it, and whether it takes you again at once when you stop.

title: A minion stops following when its target changes
assumed: A minion following a shaper stops at once when it loses that shaper or another target comes into reach, and walks back to its lane.
lookFor: Whether minions turn back at once when you lead them into the jungle or into tall grass and they lose you.

title: When a minion or tower gives up a chase
assumed: Minions and towers drop a target within about half a second when it leaves their range or their area, or hides in fog or tall grass.
lookFor: How far a minion follows you off its lane, and whether minions or a tower stop hitting you at once when you step into tall grass.

title: Minions in the enemy base
assumed: Minions that reach the enemy base attack the nearest core or the Guardian and stay on them, taking on only enemies that come near.
lookFor: Which core minions hit first when they break into a base, and whether they leave the cores to chase a shaper.

title: The order of an empowered wave
assumed: An empowered wave after the parasite's last stage spawns its big Strider first, then three melee minions, then three casters, half a second apart.
lookFor: Whether the Strider of an empowered wave comes out first or last.

title: Who a Binding shoots
assumed: A Binding shoots minions before shapers, but switches to a shaper who hurts an allied shaper in its range and keeps shooting that shaper until it leaves the range.
lookFor: Whom a Binding shoots when minions and shapers stand in its range, and how long it keeps shooting a shaper who hit one of its team's shapers.

title: No tier protection for Bindings
assumed: Every Binding can be attacked at any time; an inner Binding has no protection while the outer one of its lane stands.
lookFor: Damage on a middle or inner Binding while the outer one of its lane still stands, or a shield on a later Binding.

title: The Guardian's shield comes back with a core
assumed: When a destroyed core regrows, the Guardian's shield comes back.
lookFor: Whether the Guardian is shielded again after all its cores fell and one of them regrew.

title: The Guardian aims at shapers
assumed: The Guardian's basic attack goes to a random enemy shaper in reach when there is one, otherwise to minions, and its special attacks aim only at shapers.
lookFor: Whether the Guardian shoots you or your minions when you stand near it beside them, and whether its specials land only on shapers.

title: Each core takes one Guardian special with it
assumed: Each of the five cores powers one of the Guardian's special attacks, which stops while that core is down, and the specials come more slowly with each lost core.
lookFor: Whether a special (such as the laser after the rear right core fell) still comes before the core regrows, and whether the defenders ever got health packs from their Guardian.

title: Well income: for every player, every second
assumed: Each worker at a well pays 1.5 gold a minute to every player of its team, paid out every second.
lookFor: The score panel's gold per minute compared with the number of wells and workers, and how fast an idle player's gold grows with full wells.

title: Who gets the capture's gold
assumed: The 50 gold for capturing a well and the well's bounty go to every player of the capturing team, even those far away.
lookFor: Whether teammates elsewhere on the map get +50 gold at a capture, and how big the bounty is.

title: What pauses a capture: an enemy shaper's hit
assumed: Only enemy shapers pause a capture: an enemy shaper's hit pauses the capturer's share for 5 seconds, while damage from workers, minions, creeps or towers does not.
lookFor: Whether a capture keeps filling while an enemy shaper hits the capturer from outside the ring, for example with a ranged poke or damage over time.

title: Workers: when they come and are replaced
assumed: A well starts with no workers and gets one more every 15 seconds from the start of the match, up to 18, and a killed worker is replaced on the same 15-second timer.
lookFor: How many workers a well has at 0:30, 1:00 and 2:00, and how soon a killed worker is replaced.

title: A capture fading after the capturers leave
assumed: An abandoned capture ring empties at the speed of a one-shaper capture, a full ring in about 16 seconds.
lookFor: How long the ring of a capture abandoned half-way takes to empty.

title: The "well under attack" alert
assumed: The "Spirit Well under attack" alert plays only when an enemy hits one of the well's workers, not when enemies just start a capture.
lookFor: Whether the alert plays when enemies start a capture without hitting a worker.

title: Gold for killing a worker: how close you must be
assumed: Killing a worker pays 6 gold and 15 XP to your team's shapers within about 16 units of it, and nothing when it is killed from farther away.
lookFor: Whether gold pops up when a worker is killed from long range.

title: Workers destroyed by a capture pay nothing
assumed: The workers that vanish when a well is captured pay no gold or XP to anyone.
lookFor: The capturers' gold at the moment of a capture.

title: Where workers mine
assumed: Each worker gathers at its own spot at the edge of the well's platform and carries the Vim to near the well's centre.
lookFor: Where workers pick up and where they drop off as they walk.

title: The unlock and lock animations
assumed: A well's dais plays its unlock animation for 2 seconds when the well opens and its lock animation for 2 seconds after a capture.
lookFor: The dais at 15:00 and right after a capture.

title: Who is named in "Spirit Well captured"
assumed: When several shapers capture a well together, the announcement names the one who comes first in the team's player order.
lookFor: Which shaper the "Spirit Well captured" announcement names when two shapers capture together.

title: A worker stays on its well's platform
assumed: A worker never chases off its well's platform: it drops a target just beyond the platform's edge and goes back to mining.
lookFor: Whether a worker steps off its platform after a shaper who hit it, and whether it hits a shaper standing just outside the ring.

title: Camp timers: the creatures' values
assumed: Small camps first appear at 1:30 and come back 3:00 after a clear, the buff camps at 1:30 and 5:00 after a clear, and the Gold Pigs at 3:30 and 5:00 after a clear.
lookFor: How soon after a clear a small camp comes back, and whether all small camps first appear at 1:30.

title: A camp's timer starts when the whole camp is dead
assumed: A camp's respawn timer starts when its last creature dies, so a camp with one creature left alive never brings the others back.
lookFor: The time from a camp's last kill to its return, and whether the others come back while one creature is left alive.

title: Who gets a jungle buff
assumed: A jungle buff goes only to the shaper who lands the last hit on the big creature and is alive then; a kill by a minion or a tower gives nobody the buff.
lookFor: Whether anyone gets the buff when a minion finishes a buff creature, and whether a teammate who is dead when the parasite dies gets the team buff.

title: The buff creature's size
assumed: A camp's big creature has its normal size, not twice the size.
lookFor: The size of the big Fish, Fungus and Ugger next to the small ones.

title: How far a camp follows you
assumed: A jungle creature follows you up to about 18 to 22 units from its spot, gives up a chase after 5 seconds without landing a hit, and then the whole camp walks home.
lookFor: How far a buff creature follows you before it turns back, and whether a ranged shaper can shoot a camp from far outside it without the camp coming out.

title: A camp's big creature walks through its small ones
assumed: A camp's big creature walks through its own small creatures to reach a shaper standing behind them.
lookFor: Whether the big creature reaches you when you stand behind one of its small camp-mates, and whether it walks through, pushes or walks around it.

title: The parasite ignores you until you hit it
assumed: The parasite attacks only those who hit it and leaves a shaper standing near it alone.
lookFor: Whether the parasite attacks someone walking close past it without attacking it.

title: Whom the parasite attacks, and its specials
assumed: Once hit, the parasite attacks the nearest enemy shaper in its melee reach, and from its second stage on every fifth attack is a special: the fire breath, and at the third stage the fire breath and the orb barrage in turn.
lookFor: A fire breath after every four attacks of a second-stage parasite, the two specials taking turns at the third stage, and whether it hits the shaper next to it rather than the one who hit it first from range.

title: The death timer
assumed: You respawn after 15 seconds plus half a second per level plus 1.25 seconds per minute of the match.
lookFor: The respawn countdown at a known level and match time.

title: Assists: 10 seconds
assumed: Every enemy who hit or debuffed the victim, or buffed a teammate who hit it, in the last 10 seconds before the kill gets an assist.
lookFor: The scoreboard's assists when someone hit the victim 8 to 12 seconds before the kill.

title: Extra damage reductions
assumed: Damage reductions such as the Orange buff's stacks, a weakening debuff on the attacker, area resistance and the bonuses against structures all apply after armor and magic resist.
lookFor: The same ability's damage number on a target with and without such an effect.

title: On-hit effects through a shield
assumed: On-hit effects of items still trigger when a shield takes the whole hit, and such a hit still cancels a recall.
lookFor: Hitting a fully shielded enemy with an on-hit item, and whether a recall stops when the enemy's shield takes the hit.

title: Where damage-changing effects act
assumed: Flat damage cuts such as Toughness's "-3 damage from basic attacks" apply after armor, while effects that change the damage a unit takes apply before it.
lookFor: A basic attack's damage number on a target with Toughness.

title: Which shield absorbs first
assumed: When a shaper has several shields, the one that runs out first absorbs first, and a magic-only shield takes magic damage before the others.
lookFor: Two shields on one shaper and which one's bar empties first.

title: Streaks and bounties
assumed: Dying several times in a row lowers your bounty step by step, only a kill (not an assist) ends that streak, and kills within 10 seconds of each other make a multi-kill.
lookFor: The gold for killing a player who died several times in a row and then got only assists.

title: Your orders end at your death
assumed: Your orders end when you die, so after the respawn your shaper stands still at the base.
lookFor: Whether a shaper who died while attacking a Binding walks back to it by itself after the respawn.

title: Small damage details
assumed: A hit on an immune target does nothing and shows "Immune", and a projectile still hits after its caster died but heals the dead caster nothing.
lookFor: The "Immune" text on an immune target, and heals from spell overload's extra hits.

title: Hits below one HP show no number
assumed: A hit that takes less than one whole point of health shows no damage number, though it still counts in full.
lookFor: The small numbers under each hit of a fast multi-hit ability, such as Faris's ranged W, and whether any of them is ever 0.

title: Drain heals its caster again
assumed: Each tick of Drain sends three small bolts back from the target and heals the caster 90 percent of the tick's damage when they arrive.
lookFor: Three small bolts flying back after each tick of Drain, and the caster's health rising by about nine tenths of each tick's damage.

title: Item passives stop at death and come back at the respawn
assumed: Item passives that end at death, such as Purity's heal and the Legendary auras, stop while you are dead and start again at once when you respawn.
lookFor: An item's aura or heal while its holder is dead, and whether it is back right after the respawn.

title: The roles' bonuses are on
assumed: The four roles' bonuses are on from the start: the Gladiator's stored minion gold, the Hunter's extra creep gold, the Predator's double worker gold and the Tactician's +20 gold for hitting an enemy shaper.
lookFor: The roles' gold popups in a match, such as the Tactician's +20 on a hit.

title: A perk page's percent stats and Spiritstone effects
assumed: A perk page's percent stats and its Spiritstones' effects are given to your shaper at the start of the match and kept through deaths.
lookFor: Your stats panel in a match compared with the loadout's statistics, and a Spiritstone's effect in play.

title: Perk effects that end at death come back at the respawn
assumed: The Vanguard Spiritstone's aura stops while you are dead and comes back when you respawn, while every other Spiritstone's effect stays through death.
lookFor: The Vanguard aura on nearby enemies after a respawn.

title: Shaper passives from the start and after each respawn
assumed: Every shaper's passive runs from the start of the match and starts again after each respawn.
lookFor: A passive's icon or effect right after a respawn.

title: Mikella's W: the coins' bonus ends with the W
assumed: A coin of Mikella's that lands after her W has ended gets no bonus.
lookFor: The damage of a coin landing just after Mikella's W ended.

title: Empathy's cooldown on the HUD
assumed: The item Empathy never shows a cooldown on the HUD.
lookFor: Whether Empathy showed a cooldown on the HUD in the original.

title: The shop's delivery comes from the nearer archon
assumed: A bought item's delivery flies from the shop archon of your base nearest to you, and that archon plays its purchase animation.
lookFor: Which archon (or both) the delivery leaves from when a shaper buys from either side of the shop.

title: A one-moment ground effect stays for a second
assumed: A ground effect that an ability makes for only an instant, such as Khagen's Q sand burst, stays on screen for one second.
lookFor: How long Khagen's Q sand burst shows, and whether it is cut short.

title: Raina's shield drains her Discipline, and drops when it runs out
assumed: Raina's W shield drains her Discipline at 12.5 a second, so a full bar lasts 8 seconds, and the shield drops when the bar runs out; raising it needs 15 Discipline but doesn't spend them.
lookFor: Raina's Discipline bar when she raises her W: whether it drops by 15 at once, how fast it falls, and whether the shield drops when it is empty.

title: A debuff's visual marker goes with the debuff
assumed: A Duress stack marker over an enemy disappears when its 4-second counter runs out, also while the enemy is in the fog.
lookFor: Whether the Duress pips vanish about 4 seconds after the last hit, or ever linger.

title: The practice match's bots
assumed: A practice match is five against five, its bots on shapers such as High Huntress, Tidal Queen, Guardian, Artist and Warden, each seat filled from the game's own bot plan.
lookFor: The bot lineup of a practice match.

title: The bots' lanes
assumed: In a practice match two bots of each team go to the top lane and three to the bottom lane.
lookFor: Where the bots go when they leave the base at about 1:05.

title: The bots' shopping
assumed: A bot buys its shaper's recommended build in order, never sells, keeps two potions, and shops whenever it stands in its shop with the gold.
lookFor: A bot's items on the scoreboard at 10:00, and whether a bot that never dies falls behind in items.

title: Bots are a little stronger
assumed: Every bot gets a small stat bonus in place of a perk page, with more power, health, haste and armor (a High Huntress bot has 628 health at level 1 instead of 520).
lookFor: A bot's health at level 1.

title: The bots' teamwork
assumed: A bot going in for a kill calls two more bots to join it.
lookFor: How many bots come to a gank or to defend a tower.

title: The bots' reaction time
assumed: A bot makes its decisions five times a second.
lookFor: How fast bots react to a stun or a dash.

title: Bots flee and dodge
assumed: Bots run from the Guardian's and the parasite's ground attacks, flee when clearly outnumbered, and chase a target up to about 55 units.
lookFor: Whether bots flee when outnumbered, and how far they chase.

title: Softer bots in a first-time game
assumed: In a player's first practice game the bots play softer against the human.
lookFor: Whether practice bots play softer in a player's first game than later.

title: The bots play as a team
assumed: Each bot team follows one plan at a time (defend the base, push a lane when it has the advantage, take the parasite together, raid an unguarded well, or farm) and pings its plans on the minimap to its human teammates.
lookFor: Whether bots take the parasite alone or as a group, when they group up to push, and whether they ping.

title: Bots recall when they get away, and step back in lane
assumed: A fleeing bot walks home until it is out of danger and then recalls, and in a lane fight a bot backs off only a short step toward its base.
lookFor: How far a fleeing bot walks before it recalls, and whether bots in lane back off a little or go home.

title: Bot pushes last, and the late siege
assumed: Bots keep a push going while they are not outnumbered, and from 20 minutes on they group up to siege the enemy base.
lookFor: Whether bots group up and siege after 20 minutes, whether they turn back to their base or keep pushing, and how soon they come again after a lost fight.

title: The bot jungler takes part
assumed: The bot jungler leaves its camps to defend its base, to join pushes, the parasite and well captures nearby, and from 3:00 to gank a lane when the odds favour it.
lookFor: How often the bot jungler shows up in a lane, and whether it comes to defend and joins pushes and objectives.

title: Bots follow your minimap pings
assumed: Bots answer your minimap pings: a ping on an enemy tower makes them push that lane, on the parasite take it, on an enemy well capture it, and on your own tower or well defend it.
lookFor: Whether bots reacted to minimap pings at all, and to which.

title: When the bot jungler takes on a shaper, and where it fights the parasite
assumed: The bot jungler attacks a lone enemy shaper it meets in the jungle unless it is outnumbered or clearly weaker, and fights the parasite from the edge on its own side.
lookFor: Whether the bot jungler attacks you when you pass it alone in the jungle at similar health, backs off when you clearly outclass it, and keeps hitting the parasite.

title: Which bots defend a spirit well, how far they come and when they give up
assumed: A nearby bot Tactician, Hunter or Predator comes to defend its team's well when enemies capture it, and leaves when it is clearly outnumbered.
lookFor: Whether a bot comes when you start capturing an enemy well near it, stays while you are in the ring, and leaves when you bring two friends.

title: The bot jungler's priorities: pushes, the base, waves, its own camps first
assumed: The bot jungler joins its team's pushes, defends the base only when it is close, farms a lane wave when no camp is near, clears its own half of the jungle first, and catches up when it falls behind in levels.
lookFor: The bot junglers' levels at 10, 15 and 20 minutes compared with their teams', and how often they join a push.

title: The bot jungler finishes a camp it is winning
assumed: A bot jungler at low health keeps fighting a camp it is winning instead of walking away from a creature at a sliver of health.
lookFor: Whether the bot jungler walks away from a camp with one creature at a sliver of health, and whether it dies to camps.

title: Bot shapers finish a fight they are winning, and no longer flicker between stances
assumed: A bot at low health finishes an enemy shaper at a sliver of health when it can win the trade, but doesn't dive a tower for a kill it can't make quickly.
lookFor: Whether a low-health bot finishes an enemy at a sliver of health, and whether it dives a tower for a kill.

title: A bot you attack shoots back while it backs off, and doesn't recall with you on it
assumed: A bot you attack shoots back at you while it backs off, and doesn't recall while you are on it.
lookFor: Whether a bot that backs off turns and shoots between its steps, and whether it starts a recall while you chase it.

title: The bot jungler's opening route and Vanquish
assumed: The bot jungler opens with a fixed route through its own jungle (the green buff, the small camps, the blue buff, then the bigger camps) until level 6 or 10 minutes.
lookFor: The bot jungler's first camps, and when it reaches level 2.

title: When a bot turns back from an enemy tower
assumed: A bot backs off from an enemy tower that hit it recently or aims at it, and leaves targets under such a tower alone unless it can finish a low-health shaper or the tower.
lookFor: Whether bots take several tower shots in a row or die chasing under a tower, and whether they hang back at a tower's edge while their minions tank it.

title: Gold for a last hit, and for standing near
assumed: A lane minion pays its last hitter three times its gold (12 for a melee minion), and every other shaper of the team nearby gets a share (4 each for a melee minion).
lookFor: The gold numbers at a last hit on a melee minion, and whether a teammate standing near gets 4.

title: How the roles' 200 % apply to minion gold
assumed: A Gladiator's last hit on a lane minion pays its bonus twice (12 + 12 for a melee minion) and a Tactician's nearby share is doubled (4 + 4), each role's part shown as a second, smaller gold number.
lookFor: The gold numbers of a Gladiator's last hit on a melee minion at level 1, and a Tactician's when a teammate last-hits a minion beside it.

title: Gold and XP for a player kill
assumed: A kill pays the killer the victim's bounty of 300 gold (more for kill streaks, less after death streaks) plus 100 for first blood, and the assisters a share of it (70 percent with one assister).
lookFor: The gold numbers at a kill, an assist and first blood.

title: Passive gold paid every second
assumed: Passive gold of 100 a minute comes in from 1:00, paid every second rather than once a minute.
lookFor: The gold counter of an idle player between 1:00 and 2:00.

title: What counts for the creep score
assumed: Only last hits on minions and jungle creeps count for the creep score, not workers, structures or the parasite.
lookFor: The creep score after killing a worker.

title: The loot bag after a match
assumed: A won first-time practice game gives the Platinum loot bag with a Spiritstone and two Sparks, any other practice game the Bronze bag, and other games the bag their score reaches.
lookFor: The loot bags and the Destiny shown after practice and player-versus-player matches.

title: Duplicate items become crafting currency
assumed: A reward item you already own turns into crafting currency: 50 for a Spiritstone, 15 for a Spark, 25 for anything else.
lookFor: The post-game screen when a reward is an item you already own.

title: Karma votes
assumed: Each karma vote you get after a player-versus-player match adds 10 points to your loot bag's score.
lookFor: The karma bonus in the Blessings view after a match.

title: How far a shaper sees
assumed: A shaper sees about 35 units around itself.
lookFor: The size of the lit circle around a shaper, on screen and on the minimap.

title: Tall grass and walls
assumed: Tall grass hides what is in it and behind it from anyone outside, and a wall hides what is behind it, as the game draws its fog.
lookFor: Whether enemies at wall corners and just behind grass are seen or not.

title: Stealth
assumed: Nothing reveals stealth: a stealthed shaper, a ward after its first seconds or a trap stays hidden from enemies even right next to them.
lookFor: Whether a stealthed shaper next to an enemy is visible, faint or hidden.

title: Wards can't be destroyed
assumed: A placed ward can't be attacked or destroyed by anyone and lasts its full three minutes.
lookFor: A player attacking an enemy ward it can see, and whether the ward takes damage or dies.

title: A death at the edge of sight
assumed: A unit you saw when it died stays visible until it is removed, so you see its whole death.
lookFor: A unit dying at the edge of your vision.

title: Objects that follow their owner's visibility
assumed: An enemy's orbs, books and crystals are seen exactly when their owner is.
lookFor: An enemy's orbiting objects while the enemy itself is hidden.

title: Large objects
assumed: A large object such as Marah's trees is seen as soon as a vision circle reaches any part of it, not only its centre.
lookFor: Marah's trees seen from a distance.

title: Sounds from the fog
assumed: You hear and see the effects, animations and hits of an object only while your team sees it, so nothing sounds from the fog.
lookFor: Whether you hear enemy units, recalls or casts that you can't see.

title: What you know of an enemy out of sight
assumed: The scoreboard shows an enemy's level, items, gold and creep score as you last saw them, and updates them the moment the enemy shows again.
lookFor: Whether an enemy who has been out of sight for a while shows its current level and items on the scoreboard, or older ones.

title: Kensu's R trail and sight
assumed: The trail of Kensu's R never blocks sight, and where it crosses a wall it opens the wall for sight while it lasts.
lookFor: Whether an enemy standing behind a wall that Kensu's trail crosses is seen through the trail.

area: Match flow: start, surrender, end, post-game
title: When a team may surrender, and the vote
assumed: A team may surrender from 20:00, or earlier when a player has been gone for 5 minutes or the team is far behind, and a vote passes with two thirds of the team.
lookFor: When the surrender option appeared in matches, and how votes ended.

area: Match flow: start, surrender, end, post-game
title: No surrender in practice games
assumed: Practice games against bots have no surrender.
lookFor: Whether the Options menu offered to surrender the game in a practice match.

area: Match flow: start, surrender, end, post-game
title: A team that left surrenders
assumed: When every player of a team has been gone for 60 seconds while the other team still has a player, that team surrenders.
lookFor: Whether a match where a whole team left ended, and when.

area: Match flow: start, surrender, end, post-game
title: The end of the post-game
assumed: The post-game ends 105 seconds after the Guardian's death if nobody clicks on.
lookFor: How long the victory screen stays when nobody clicks.

area: Match flow: start, surrender, end, post-game
title: Custom games end like a lost practice game
assumed: A custom game ends like a lost practice game: its end screen and rewards come at once, with no karma vote.
lookFor: The end screens of a custom game.

area: Match flow: start, surrender, end, post-game
title: Karma votes for bots
assumed: The karma vote offers the bots, but a vote for a bot counts for nobody, and bots never vote.
lookFor: Whether bots appeared in the karma vote, and what a vote for one did.

title: The "Match Found — accept" prompt
assumed: A matchmade game starts without the "Match Found, accept" prompt.
lookFor: Whether "Match Found, click accept to join" appeared in videos of the player-versus-player queue.

title: No rejoin after a drop in shaper select
assumed: A player who drops during shaper select is not offered to rejoin; only one who drops during the match is.
lookFor: A disconnect during shaper select, and whether a Rejoin button was offered.

title: The bots' picks
assumed: The bots pick their shapers one after another within the first few seconds of shaper select.
lookFor: When the bots lock in their shapers in a practice match's shaper select.

title: Spectators
assumed: A spectator of a custom game sees both teams without fog of war, and the players' screens list who is watching.
lookFor: A spectator's screen, and whether the players saw who watched.

title: Ward skins and announcer packs for everyone
assumed: In shaper select every account can pick any ward skin and announcer pack, owned or not.
lookFor: Whether an account that didn't own a ward skin could pick one in shaper select.

title: The minion announcements
assumed: The announcer warns about the minions at 0:30, half a minute before the first wave, and announces them as the first wave spawns at 1:00.
lookFor: The announcer at the start of a match.

title: Jungle camp icons show what your team knows; the parasite's while it lives
assumed: A jungle camp's minimap icon shows what your team knows: no icon before the first spawn, gone when your team sees the camp cleared, back when it respawns; the parasite's icon shows while it lives.
lookFor: Whether the camp icons showed before the first spawn, whether a camp's icon went away when you cleared it and stayed when the enemy cleared it unseen, and whether the parasite's icon is there before it is born at 5:00.

title: No number when a shield goes up
assumed: No number pops up when a shield is put on a unit.
lookFor: Whether a number pops up when a shield is cast.

title: Who hears voice lines
assumed: Quick-chat callouts go only to your team, while laugh, joke, compliment, flirt, taunt and dance lines are heard by everyone.
lookFor: Whether you hear an enemy's laugh or callout in a video from the other team's side.

title: The shapers' banter
assumed: Two shapers who know each other exchange a line near each other at the start of a match, and a kill gives a line from the killer and one assister, heard while your team sees the speaker.
lookFor: The shapers' lines at the start of a match and at kills.

title: "Player left" and "reconnected" alerts
assumed: The "player left" and "reconnected" alerts go to everyone in the match, both teams.
lookFor: Whether the other team sees that someone left.

title: The respawn voice line
assumed: Your shaper's respawn line plays only for you, and a bot's respawn plays no line.
lookFor: Whether you heard an ally's respawn line.

title: The death recap
assumed: The death recap shows the hits of the fight that killed you, up to 30 seconds back to the first pause of 5 seconds, with the most recent sources first.
lookFor: A death recap after a long fight.

title: The HUD's Binding icons
assumed: The top bar's Binding icons are ordered top lane first, outer before middle before inner.
lookFor: Whether the right icon on the top bar is marked after the top outer Binding falls.

title: The HUD's well icons
assumed: The top bar's four well icons are in a fixed order that we picked from the map.
lookFor: The top bar's well icons compared with the wells on the map.

title: Death animations
assumed: A critical killing blow shows a critical death, an area or damage-over-time kill its own death, and a knockback kill a knockback death.
lookFor: The death animations of critical kills and knockback kills.

title: Prices of Spiritstones and Sparks
assumed: A Spiritstone costs 500 Destiny and a Spark 150 in the store.
lookFor: The store prices of Spiritstones and Sparks in videos or screenshots.

title: How many perk pages
assumed: A player can own up to 10 perk pages.
lookFor: How many loadout pages a player could own.

title: No bots in custom games
assumed: A custom game has only the players its lobby gathered, with no bots.
lookFor: Whether custom games in videos had bots.

title: Which error a refused purchase shows
assumed: A refused store purchase shows the client's error message that fits best.
lookFor: The error popups of the original store.

title: A disabled or banned player is thrown out without a message
assumed: A player who is banned or disabled during a session is sent back to an empty login screen without a message, and sees the reason only at the next login.
lookFor: What a player banned during a session saw.

title: The filled "Starter" perk page
assumed: A new account's first perk page, "Starter", is filled with a blue, a green and two red starter Spiritstones, each with its colour's plain Spark.
lookFor: A new account's Loadouts screen.

title: Regeneration in half-second steps
assumed: Health and resources regenerate in steps every half second, and the dead regenerate nothing.
lookFor: Whether the health number rises smoothly, every half second or every second while regenerating.

title: Lane casters' reach
assumed: Lane casters walk up to about 15 units from their target before they shoot.
lookFor: How far casters stand from their target.

title: A command on a target that just died or vanished into fog
assumed: An ability or ping on a target that just died, or that vanished from view more than 2 seconds ago, simply doesn't happen, with no error text.
lookFor: Whether clicking an ability on an enemy the moment it dies or steps into a bush shows an error text or nothing.
